Let $u=5-3x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6(5-3x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int 6{u}^{2}\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})\,\text{d}u \\  & =6\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})\int {u}^{2}\cdot \,\text{d}u \\  & =-2\int {u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{{u}^{3}}{3}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}(5-3x)^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-\frac{2}{3}(5-3x)^{3}+C] & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{2}{3}(5-3x)^{3}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-2(5-3x)^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-3x)+0 \\  & =-2(5-3x)^{2}\cdot (-3) \\  & =6(5-3x)^{2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
